name: OpenAI Build Week
theme: Global online hackathon to build working projects with Codex and GPT-5.6 across consumer life apps, work/productivity, developer tools, and education.
team_size: No limit on team size according to FAQ; entrants may participate as individuals, teams, or organizations. Some prize benefits are capped, including up to two DevDay/Exchange passes for 1st-place teams.
required_or_encouraged_tech: /feedback Codex Session ID required from the primary build thread
Public YouTube demo video under 3 minutes with audio explaining use of Codex and GPT-5.6
Code repository URL required; public with relevant licensing or private shared with testing@devpost.com and build-week-event@openai.com
README with setup instructions, sample data if needed, run/test guidance, Codex workflow, key decisions, and GPT-5.6/Codex contribution
Standard libraries, frameworks, third-party SDKs/APIs/data allowed if authorized and licensed
prizes: 1st Place | Apps for Your Life: $15,000 cash, up to two DevDay/Exchange passes, OpenAI Developers promotion, meeting with Codex Team, Pro Account for 1 year
2nd Place | Apps for Your Life: $10,000 cash, OpenAI Developers promotion, Pro Account for 1 year
1st Place | Work & Productivity: $15,000 cash, up to two DevDay/Exchange passes, OpenAI Developers promotion, meeting with Codex Team, Pro Account for 1 year
2nd Place | Work & Productivity: $10,000 cash, OpenAI Developers promotion, Pro Account for 1 year
1st Place | Developer Tools: $15,000 cash, up to two DevDay/Exchange passes, OpenAI Developers promotion, meeting with Codex Team, Pro Account for 1 year
2nd Place | Developer Tools: $10,000 cash, OpenAI Developers promotion, Pro Account for 1 year
1st Place | Education: $15,000 cash, up to two DevDay/Exchange passes, OpenAI Developers promotion, meeting with Codex Team, Pro Account for 1 year
2nd Place | Education: $10,000 cash, OpenAI Developers promotion, Pro Account for 1 year
Each project is eligible for one prize

facts.claim: Registration runs July 9, 2026 10:00 PT to July 21, 2026 17:00 PT; submission period runs July 13, 2026 09:00 PT to July 21, 2026 17:00 PT.
The schedule page lists submissions ending July 21, 2026 17:00 PDT, judging July 22, 2026 09:00 PDT to August 09, 2026 17:00 PDT, and winners announced August 12, 2026 14:00 PDT.
The official rules list judging as July 22, 2026 10:00 PT to August 5, 2026 17:00 PT, creating a discrepancy with the schedule page.

Eligible entrants include individuals at least the age of majority in their residence, eligible teams, and eligible organizations in OpenAI API-supported countries or territories, subject to exclusions.

Excluded entrants include unsupported or prohibited jurisdictions, including examples Brazil, Quebec, Russia, Crimea, Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Syria, and other OFAC-designated countries, plus promotion entities, judges, related affiliates, and conflicts of interest.
Projects must be built with Codex and GPT-5.6 and fit one of four tracks: Apps for Your Life, Work and Productivity, Developer Tools, or Education.
Submitted projects must install and run consistently on their intended platform and function as shown in the demo or described in text.

Pre-existing projects are allowed only if meaningfully extended using Codex and/or GPT-5.6 after the submission period start; prior work versus new work must be documented with evidence such as logs or commit history.
Third-party SDKs, APIs, and data are allowed only when the entrant is authorized to use them under applicable terms or licenses.
Submission requires a text description, category, demo video under three minutes, public YouTube link, code repository URL, README, and /feedback Codex Session ID.
The demo video must include a clear demo with audio covering what was built and how Codex and GPT-5.6 were used; judges are not required to watch beyond three minutes.
Judges may test the project but are not required to; they may judge solely from submission text, images, and video.
For plugins or developer tools, submissions must include installation instructions, supported platforms, and a testing path such as a demo instance, sandbox, or test account.
The README guidance says Codex collaboration, workflow acceleration, key decisions, and GPT-5.6/Codex contributions are important to Technical Implementation and Quality of the Idea judging.

Stage One is a pass/fail viability screen for theme fit and use of required APIs/SDKs; Stage Two uses equally weighted criteria: Technological Implementation, Design, Potential Impact, and Quality of the Idea.
Tie-breaks compare the tied submissions by the first listed criterion, then subsequent criteria, then judge vote if still tied.
The Devpost Hackathons Plugin is optional and is explicitly not the official source of hackathon information; official rules, website, updates, and notices prevail.
The resources page says all available $100 Codex credits had been given out, while participants could still join using the free tier.
The resources page encourages starting with the problem, keeping the repo testable, recording the demo as work progresses, and watching credit usage.
The FAQ says each project can be entered into only one track and entrants should choose the closest match.
The FAQ says Free plan users can participate and have access to GPT-5.6 Terra in Codex; GPT-5.6 need only be used for part of the project.
OpenAI Help says GPT-5.6 in Codex includes Terra for Free and Go, and Sol, Terra, and Luna for Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise, while OpenAI API availability includes Sol, Terra, and Luna.
OpenAI Help describes Codex as an AI coding agent that can help write, review, and ship code, including pairing locally or delegating work in the cloud.
OpenAI Help describes Codex CLI as a command-line coding agent that can read, modify, and run code locally, with multimodal inputs and an approvals workflow.
The project gallery page had not been published at browse time, so no current submissions, finalists, or winners were available there.

inference.claim: Technical Implementation is strategically the most important criterion despite equal weights because it is the first tie-break criterion and is reinforced by required Codex/GPT-5.6 evidence in the README, video, and /feedback Session ID.
inference.rationale: Rules state equal weighting but tie-breaks start with the first listed criterion; submission requirements repeatedly require specific evidence of Codex and GPT-5.6 use.

inference.claim: Complete runnable product experience is likely a stronger lane than pure model demo because Design explicitly penalizes technical proofs of concept and testing access may determine whether judges can verify function quickly.
inference.rationale: Design criterion asks for a complete coherent product experience, and rules say judges may rely on demo/text if they do not test.

inference.claim: Projects that expose Codex as a visible build accelerator or audit trail may align better with sponsor priorities than projects where model use is hidden.
inference.rationale: README and video must explain where Codex accelerated workflow, key decisions, and GPT-5.6/Codex contribution.

inference.claim: Underrepresented workflows should emphasize irreversible workflow outcomes, constraint handling, testability, and failure prevention rather than chat wrappers or dashboards.
inference.rationale: Judging asks for working non-trivial implementation, credible real-world impact, and novelty; default seed blacklist identifies saturated archetypes.

judging_criteria.name: Stage One viability screen
judging_criteria.notes: Project must reasonably fit the theme and reasonably apply the required APIs/SDKs featured in the hackathon.

judging_criteria.name: Technological Implementation
judging_criteria.weight_or_priority: Equal Stage Two weight; first tie-break priority
judging_criteria.notes: Assesses thorough and skillful Codex use, genuine effort, and working non-trivial implementation.

judging_criteria.name: Design
judging_criteria.weight_or_priority: Equal Stage Two weight; second tie-break priority
judging_criteria.notes: Assesses whether the project is working/runnable with a complete coherent product experience, not merely a technical proof of concept.

judging_criteria.name: Potential Impact
judging_criteria.weight_or_priority: Equal Stage Two weight; third tie-break priority
judging_criteria.notes: Assesses credible, specific real-audience problem framing and whether the demonstrated solution addresses it.

judging_criteria.name: Quality of the Idea
judging_criteria.weight_or_priority: Equal Stage Two weight; fourth tie-break priority
judging_criteria.notes: Assesses creativity, novelty, and difference from existing concepts.

sanitized_brief: Build a working, runnable project using Codex and GPT-5.6 for exactly one track: Apps for Your Life, Work and Productivity, Developer Tools, or Education. Stage One is pass/fail for theme fit and required tool use; Stage Two criteria are equally weighted: Technological Implementation, Design, Potential Impact, and Quality of the Idea, with tie-break priority following that order. Submissions need a text description, public under-3-minute YouTube demo with audio explaining Codex and GPT-5.6 use, repository access, README with setup/test instructions and sample data if needed, and a /feedback Codex Session ID. Sponsor capabilities to foreground are Codex as a coding agent across app/CLI/IDE/SDK workflows, GPT-5.6 integration, testable repos, demo/sandbox/test-account access, and optional Devpost plugin/community support. Blacklist labels: generic chatbot wrapper, AI study tutor/quiz/flashcards, mental-health companion, resume optimizer, PDF summarizer, meeting notes bot, recommendation-only list, dashboard-only analytics, generic opportunity navigator, crisis tip sheet, sales SDR automation, and structural twins that only rank/draft from PDFs or label uploaded CSVs.
